title: 清平调·其一
author: 李白
intro: Written on the spot for the emperor and his beloved Yang Guifei as they admired peonies, this quatrain praises a woman and a flower at the same time — so smoothly you can’t tell where one ends and the other begins.
analysis: 传说唐玄宗和杨贵妃在宫中沉香亭赏牡丹，叫李白当场写新歌词，李白写了三首《清平调》，这是第一首。第一句非常有名：“云想衣裳花想容”——看到云，就想到她的衣裳；看到花，就想到她的容貌。也可以理解为：云想要像她的衣裳，花想要像她的容貌。一句话里，人、云、花互相比喻，分不清是在写人还是写花。第二句写春风吹过栏杆，花上的露水又多又亮，暗写牡丹正盛开，也暗写贵妃受到宠爱。后两句说：这样的美人，不是在仙山群玉山上才能见到，就是在瑶台的月光下才能遇到——直接把她比作天上的仙女。全诗不说一个“美”字，却写尽了美，想象丰富，语言华丽又自然。
analysisEn: The story goes that Emperor Xuanzong and his consort Yang Guifei were admiring peonies in the palace when he summoned Li Bai to write new song lyrics on the spot. Li Bai produced three “Qingping Songs”; this is the first. Its opening line is famous for being two things at once: 云想衣裳花想容 can mean “clouds make me think of her dress, flowers of her face” — or “the clouds long to be her dress, the flowers long to be her face”. Woman, cloud and flower blur into one another, and we can’t tell whether the poem is about the lady or the peony. Line two shows the spring breeze brushing the railing and dew sparkling thick on the petals: the peonies are at their peak — and so, quietly, is the emperor’s favour towards her. The last two lines say that someone like this could only be seen on the Mountain of Jade or met under the moon at the Jasper Terrace, both homes of goddesses in legend. The poem never uses the word “beautiful”; it simply keeps comparing her to lovelier and lovelier things until she is no longer of this world.
background: Li Bai (701–762) served briefly at court in Chang’an as a poet attending the emperor, around 742–744. The occasion described — peony viewing at the Aloeswood Pavilion — comes from a Tang anecdote and is traditionally accepted, though details may be embellished.
pronunciation: 拂槛 fú jiàn（槛：栏杆，不读 kǎn）；衣裳 yī cháng（诗词逐字注音读 cháng，口语读 yīshang）。
version: 采用通行文本，组诗三首中的第一首。无重要异文。

lines.py: yún xiǎng yī cháng huā xiǎng róng
lines.lit: Clouds make me think of her clothes, flowers of her face;
lines.en: Clouds dream of being her gown, and flowers of being her face;

lines.py: chūn fēng fú jiàn lù huá nóng
lines.lit: the spring wind brushes the railing, the dew’s brightness is thick.
lines.en: the spring breeze strokes the railing, and the petals glisten with dew.

lines.py: ruò fēi qún yù shān tóu jiàn
lines.lit: If not seen on the top of the Mountain of Many Jades,
lines.en: If you have not glimpsed her on the Mountain of Jade,

lines.py: huì xiàng yáo tái yuè xià féng
lines.lit: you would meet her under the moon at the Jasper Terrace.
lines.en: you will meet her by moonlight on the Jasper Terrace of the gods.

words.en: (here) to remind one of; to long to be like
words.note: 现代汉语“想”的意思更窄，多指思考、想要。
现代汉语口语仍说“衣裳”。古代“衣”指上衣，“裳”指下裙。
现代汉语书面语“春风拂面”。
这里读 jiàn，指栏杆；读 kǎn 时是“门槛”。
华：光彩。现代汉语“光华”“华丽”。
现代汉语也说“浓茶”“浓雾”。
书面语，现代汉语说“如果不是”。

words.en: the Mountain of Many Jades (home of the Queen Mother of the West)
words.note: 神话中西王母住的仙山。
现代汉语“会”也有“一定会”的意思。

words.en: Jasper Terrace, a home of immortals

words.note: 现代汉语“相逢”“每逢佳节”。

imagery.name: 云
imagery.zh: 轻柔飘逸的云，用来比喻贵妃的衣裳。
imagery.en: Soft, drifting clouds are compared to her flowing gown.

imagery.name: 花
imagery.zh: 盛开的牡丹和美人的容貌互相比喻，花就是人，人就是花。
imagery.en: The peony in full bloom and the woman’s face mirror each other — the flower is her, and she is the flower.

imagery.name: 露
imagery.zh: 花上浓浓的露水让牡丹更加鲜艳，也暗示她正受到恩宠。
imagery.en: Thick dew makes the peonies glow even brighter — a hint that she is basking in the emperor’s favour.

imagery.name: 春风
imagery.zh: 春风吹拂栏杆，营造出宫中温暖、繁华的气氛。
imagery.en: The spring breeze over the railing sets a warm, luxurious palace mood.
